The group moves at a slow pace but with few chances to sit down for long.
458957.perChi: Perfect if you speak English and want to eat dinner on foot on your first evening in town, as a couple or with friends. Also good if you're short on time, because it combines tastings and the old town in one afternoon. Not suitable for vegans, coeliacs or the lactose intolerant, nor for wheelchair users; vegetarians must let them know in advance. If you have a nut allergy, watch out for cross-contamination.
458957.consiglio: Arrive on an empty stomach and skip lunch, because portions are bigger than you'd expect. Comfortable shoes: you're standing and on paving stones for over two hours. If you book the late-afternoon slot, you can visit the Archaeological Museum beforehand, a step from Piazza Bellini.

faq.q: What language is the tour in?
faq.a: English only. The guide talks about the food and the monuments in English throughout, for about two and a half hours. If someone in your group doesn't follow English well, they'll still enjoy the food, but will miss the explanations about the recipes and the history of the Decumani.

faq.q: What do we eat and what's included?
faq.a: The guide and all the tastings are included: taralli, frittatina, mozzarella, pizza fritta, babà, gelato and other bites, plus a spritz and a sip of limoncello. Tips aren't included. If you have particular dietary needs, flag them before booking.

faq.q: Where do we meet and where do we finish?
faq.a: You start in Piazza Bellini, next to the Greek walls, and finish in Piazza del Gesù, about ten minutes' walk from the starting point. Cancellation is free up to 24 hours before, with a full refund.

465552.intro: A three-hour trip round the bay on an old lifeboat restored to new, with a guide telling the myths and legends of Naples as you cruise along Posillipo, and stops for swimming and snorkelling. Gear included, with a wetsuit in the colder months, plus an aperitivo with beer and snacks on board. Departures in the morning, the afternoon and, in summer, early evening too. You can choose a shared or private tour.
cosaSiFa: You board the vintage boat and head out towards the Posillipo hill. Along the way the guide tells the city's legends and the stories behind the places you see from the water, while the skipper keeps to the coast. It's the time to ask questions and see the city from a side you can't see on foot.

Below Posillipo you stop for the first swim: mask and snorkel are provided, plus a wetsuit in the colder months. Non-swimmers can get in the water around the boat with flotation aids. Then you carry on to Villa Lauro, where you snorkel and land on a little beach with a spring of drinkable mineral water.

On the way back comes the aperitivo: a beer, a snack and the view across the bay. There's an extra drink if you want one. You're back at the starting point after about three hours, on the shared or private option you chose when booking.
465552.perChi: For anyone who only has a weekend but still wants the sea and a boat without going as far as the islands; for couples and groups of friends, with the private option if there are lots of you. Not allowed: children under two, pregnant women, anyone weighing over 130 kg, anyone over 70 or with pre-existing medical conditions.
465552.consiglio: Wear your swimsuit from home, and bring a towel, hat and sun cream: the sun on the water is fierce. If you get seasick, bring something to take before boarding. In summer the 6pm departure has the best light on the bay. The exact meeting point comes after booking and depends on the option chosen.

faq.q: What's included?
faq.a: The guide, snorkelling gear with a wetsuit in the colder months, the aperitivo with beer and snacks, and an extra drink. The trip lasts three hours and can be booked shared or private, depending on how many of you there are.

faq.q: What language is it in, and can I cancel?
faq.a: English, Italian and Spanish. Free cancellation up to 24 hours before with a full refund, and you can book now and pay later.

faq.q: What time does it leave and what should I bring?
faq.a: Departures are at 10:30am and 2:30pm, and in summer also at 6pm. Bring a swimsuit, towel, hat and sun protection. If you get seasick, bring medication. The meeting point depends on the option booked.

486452.intro: An evening round the bars of the old town and the Quartieri Spagnoli (the Spanish Quarter) with a guide and a group of strangers who won't be strangers by the end of the night. You start at Toledo metro station, hit three or four bars, listen to street musicians in the squares and play ice-breaker games. It's over-18s only and lasts about two and a half hours, rain or shine.
cosaSiFa: Meet in front of Toledo metro station, on Via Toledo. From there you walk towards the old town. The group stops at three or four bars chosen because Neapolitans actually drink there and prices are local; the guide points out the best deals and tells you where it's worth paying cash.

Between bars you cross the squares where street musicians play in the evening, and the guide gets everyone playing group games, some of them fairly odd, to get strangers talking. The route goes as far as the Quartieri Spagnoli. If you're hungry, grab a pizza a portafoglio (a pizza folded in four) on the street.

If you want a late one, at the end of the crawl you can be taken to a nightclub, with a separate entry fee paid on the door that includes a cocktail. Drinks along the way are paid for at the bar. About 150 minutes in all.
486452.perChi: For solo travellers or couples who want to meet people, and for groups of friends who don't know where to go on their first night. Over-18s only. Not for anyone after a quiet evening or wanting to learn the history of the lanes: here you drink, play games and walk. Sandals and flip-flops aren't allowed.
486452.consiglio: Have dinner first, or factor in a pizza a portafoglio: it's a boozy outing. Carry cash for the best deals. Toledo metro is easy to reach and, before you start, the station itself and Via Toledo are worth a look. Book ahead at weekends, it fills up.

faq.q: Where do we meet and how long does it last?
faq.a: The meeting point is Toledo metro station, in central Naples. The crawl lasts about 150 minutes, is done on foot and goes ahead in any weather, rain included.

faq.q: Are drinks included?
faq.a: The booking platform lists the guide and drinks as included, but the tour description makes clear that drinks and shots are paid for at the bars, where you'll find deals at local prices. Entry to the optional nightclub at the end is extra. Check what's included when you book.

faq.q: Minimum age, languages and cancellation?
faq.a: Over-18s only: under-18s can't take part. The guide speaks English and Italian. Cancel for free up to 24 hours before with a full refund. No sandals or flip-flops.
